subject: DPA: decommission scenarios & residency impact — request for playbook
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <gdpr@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA: decommission scenarios & residency impact — request for playbook

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As we're starting the DPA redline pass, Acme legal has asked for a concrete "decommission" playbook and a residency/retention impact matrix we can attach to the contract appendix. Our asks are: 

- A short operational playbook describing steps for primary data deletion, backups/snapshots, and certifying erasure (what evidence you can provide).
- A matrix that maps data categories to retention windows, expected time-to-delete (primary vs. backups), and jurisdictional residency behaviors (onshore copies, cross-border backups).
- Clarification on backup retention during legal hold and whether you provide certified erase proofs for backups or only for primary stores.
- Any standard SLA language you propose for deletion/erasure (we need a starting point for our counsel).

I've attached our working DPA appendix (Acme_DPA_Appendix_v3.pdf) — the redline will reference these scenarios. Can you share a draft playbook and a matrix by EOD Tuesday? If helpful, we can set a short 30-minute call.

Also, confirm whether you support a 2-step onshore purge for certain EU-only datasets (i.e., primary wipe + coordinated onshore backup purge executed by support runbook).

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Data Privacy Lead, Acme Corp
GDPR: gdpr@acme-corp.com

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Appendix_v3.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <gdpr@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA: decommission scenarios & residency impact — request for playbook

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the appendix. I've attached an internal draft playbook (redwood_decommission_playbook_v0.1.pdf) and a first-pass residency/retention matrix (residency_impact_matrix.csv). The draft is intentionally operational and highlights the steps we take across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. High-level points:

- Primary deletion: we can typically remove primary tenant data and metadata within 24-72 hours after a validated request; evidence delivered as deletion event IDs + manifest hash.
- Backup retention: backups/snapshots are handled on a tiered TTL (defaults in matrix) — long-lived backups may exist up to 90 days depending on customer configuration and region. We have a separate certified-erase workflow for onshore backup purges but timeline depends on snapshot propagation and legal hold flags.
- Jurisdictional onshore purge: supported via our Private deployment workflows or via a coordinated runbook for Dedicated customers.

Questions for Acme:
1) Which datasets do you want classified as "EU-only" (examples: user PII, customer prompts, embeddings, telemetry)?
2) Will you require us to initiate onshore backup purges or will Acme coordinate with an onshore partner?

I'll loop in Laura for contract language and Marissa for the implementation details that affect the timelines. If you'd like a short call, propose 30 Aug 10:00am PT / 6:00pm CET and we'll confirm.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

On Tue, 30 Aug 2028 at 11:05, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Appreciate the clear asks and the appendix. I've attached an internal draft playbook ...

Elena, Mina —

Thanks for the artifacts in advance. I've reviewed Mina's draft and have a few proposed DPA clause formulations to reduce ambiguity and speed negotiation. High-level suggestions below (I'll prepare a short redline document):

1) Certified Erasure Definition: propose a two-tier definition in the DPA — (a) "Primary Erasure" = deletion from live/primary stores with event manifest and deletion ID issued within 30 calendar days; (b) "Backup Erasure" = purge of removable backup media/snapshots within 90 calendar days, subject to reasonable operational constraints (snapshot compaction windows).

2) Backup Carveout & Legal Hold: include explicit language that legal holds suspend backup purges; however, Redwood will provide an evidence ledger of retained snapshots and a projected purge timeline once the hold lifts.

3) Jurisdictional Onshore Purge: for EU-only residency requests, allow the customer to select (i) Redwood Private deployment with onshore wipe capability, or (ii) a Redwood-coordinated onshore purge runbook executed with a qualified third-party onshore operator. Specify SLA windows (primary: 30 days, backup onshore purge: 30–90 days).

4) Audit & Evidence: define minimal acceptable erase evidence (manifest hash, event ID, timestamp, operator runbook reference). Add the option for audited attestation (additional fee).

5) Escrow/Third-Party Custody: if the customer requires escrow or long-term custody during dispute resolution, include a carveout and a process for transferring custody on mutually agreed terms.

I'll attach a short doc with proposed clause language (dpa_clause_suggestions.docx). Mina — if you can confirm the operational feasibility of the 30/90 windows (or propose alternate numeric bounds) I'll bake those numbers into the DPA redline.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: dpa_clause_suggestions.docx

Subject: Re: DPA: decommission scenarios & residency impact — request for playbook

Elena —

Looping in operational specifics that map to the proposed 30/90 timeline. Forwarding Mina's two attachments below for context.

Operational notes (implementation perspective):
- Snapshots: default snapshot TTL in Hosted is 90 days. For Dedicated we can configure per-deployment TTLs down to 7 days, but that requires a config change and an agreed maintenance window to expunge existing snapshots.
- Deletion workflow: we run a validated job that removes tenant keys, clears object-store pointers, and issues a deletion manifest. For backups we attach a purge job that marks snapshots for compaction; actual physical overwrite depends on underlying storage provider (S3 lifecycle vs on-prem SAN).
- Evidence: we can provide a signed manifest (SHA256 hashes), a deletion-event ID, and a snapshot index showing the purge marker. If Acme needs an independent attestation, we can provide a SOC-style supplemental attestation for a fee and time-bound schedule.

Suggested next steps:
1) Acme to mark which dataset classes require "EU-only" residency in the attached matrix.
2) Redwood to produce a final operational playbook (we'll iterate on the doc linked below).
3) Legal redline meeting — propose 31 Aug 10:00am PT / 6:00pm CET or 1 Sep 09:00am PT.

Drive link with live playbook & redline: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AaBB-example-playbook
Related ticket: JIRA INF-4572 (internal implementation request).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
